subject: Cortex Private Deploy — secure enclave topology & attestation request
summary: Nimbus asked for a concise topology and SOC2/SIG/CAIQ evidence package for a Private (VPC) deployment. Provided topology, KMS/HSM boundaries, and a SIG/CAIQ answer workbook; proposed a short technical call and identified next steps for attestation signatures.
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@nimbus-tech.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: security@nimbus-tech.com
Date: 2026-07-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: topology and attestation materials for Private deployment evaluation

Hi Hannah,

We're evaluating Redwood for a private deployment of our Cortex product and need to validate network and control-plane separation as part of our SOC 2 and SIG review. Can you provide: a high-level topology diagram showing DMZs, control-plane vs data-plane boundaries, KMS/HSM boundaries, example egress flows, and a one-page narrative describing how Dedicated vs Private isolates tenant traffic?

Specifically, our security team will want: a PDF diagram we can attach to our SIG, a CAIQ/SIG spreadsheet with answers for the Private deployment profile, and any short notes on audit logging, key management, and egress filtering.

Timeline: we are gating a short security review next week (week of 2026-07-26). Is it possible to get initial artifacts by end of day 2026-07-21?

Thanks,
Alice Tan
Senior Security Engineer, Nimbus Technologies
security@nimbus-tech.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@nimbus-tech.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: topology and attestation materials for Private deployment evaluation

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can put together the artifacts you listed. Plan:

- Deliverables by 2026-07-21 EOD (as requested): a PDF topology, a SIG/CAIQ answer workbook scoped to the Private deployment, and a short narrative (1–2 pages) describing control-plane/data-plane isolation and egress controls.
- Attachments we will include: topology diagram (PDF + SVG), KMS boundary matrix (CSV), SIG/CAIQ answers (Excel).
- Quick call: would a 30-minute sync on Tue 2026-07-20 at 09:30 PT to confirm scope and any Nimbus-specific controls be helpful? Kimberly (security architecture) and Jordan (solutions engineering) will join.

If that timing works, Kimberly will attach the initial topology and notes right after the call. If you have a template SIG row or particular CAIQ sections to prioritize, please send them over.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@nimbus-tech.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: topology and attestation materials for Private deployment evaluation

Hi Alice / Hannah — following up from our proposed agenda and scope. I attached the first-pass artifacts (see attachment list). Key points summarized below for the SIG narrative and the SOC2 control owners: 

1) Deployment model and topology (attachment: cortex-private-topology-v1.pdf)
   - Private deployment runs in a customer VPC under a customer-owned account or a dedicated VPC in the customer's cloud tenancy (per contract option).
   - Control plane (Redwood control-plane services) runs in a separate VPC/region and is logically isolated by VPC peering with strict route tables and security groups. No direct write access from control-plane to customer data stores; only authenticated management APIs over mutual TLS.

2) DMZ and data-plane separation
   - Ingress passes through a hardened edge (WAF + rate-limiting) into a publicly facing DMZ subnet. Tokenized requests are forwarded to tenant-specific inference pools (data-plane) that are isolated by security groups and namespace-level fencing.

3) KMS/HSM and key boundaries (attachment: kms-boundary-matrix.csv)
   - Customer-managed KMS is supported. Keys may be customer-owned (preferred for Private) in their cloud KMS/HSM. Where Redwood manages keys (rare, enterprise), keys are stored in an HSM-backed managed KMS with strict role-based access and audit logging. Key usage is limited to in-memory decryption on compute nodes; private keys never persist on disk.

4) Egress filtering and logging
   - Egress to external endpoints is restricted by egress allowlists and NAT gateway policies. Per-tenant egress policies can be configured, and all flows are captured in VPC flow logs + centralized audit pipeline. Audit logs (management API, control-plane actions, and data-plane invocation logs) are retained per contract (default 90 days) and exportable to customer SIEM via secure syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver integration.

5) SIG/CAIQ workbook (attachment: sig-caIQ-answers-2026.xlsx)
   - Workbook includes mappings for the Private deployment profile. We've annotated answers where behavior differs from Hosted (notably KMS ownership and network tenancy). Please flag any question IDs you want to escalate for formal attestation.

Next steps:
- If Nimbus can confirm whether you want customer-owned KMS or Redwood-managed keys we'll mark the CAIQ accordingly.
- We can produce a short, signed attestation statement once the workbook is finalized (2–3 business days) and arrange DocuSign routing for exec signature.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@nimbus-tech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T07:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: topology and attestation materials for Private deployment evaluation

Hannah / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. I reviewed the topology and the SIG workbook briefly. A few follow-ups: 

- We will use our customer-owned KMS (AWS KMS with CloudHSM) and would like the CAIQ to reflect that.
- Can you highlight which SIG questions you mark as "requires attestation" vs "self-attested" so we can prioritize legal review?
- Please route the signed attestation via DocuSign once the workbook is finalized — we aim to include the signed statement in our vendor risk package by 2026-07-28.

I'll run this past our security manager and get back with any clarifications by EOD 2026-07-22.

Thanks again,
Alice
Senior Security Engineer, Nimbus Technologies
